findings.title: slice(1, ...) drops the newest invoice and returns a short page
findings.explanation: `rows.slice(1, limit + 1)` starts at index 1, so the first (newest) row is skipped on every page. Each page also returns only `limit - 1` items when more rows exist. When `rows.length <= limit`, the first invoice is still dropped. With a single invoice, `page` is empty. Use `rows.slice(0, limit)`.

findings.title: next_before can crash or point at the wrong row
findings.explanation: `page[page.length - 1]` depends on the faulty slice. If `limit` is 1 and there are 2 rows, `page` is `[rows[1]]`. The cursor is then the second row's id, so the skipped rows are lost. In other cases the cursor is derived from the wrong slice. After fixing the slice to `slice(0, limit)`, `page[page.length - 1].id` is correct and `page` is never empty when `hasMore` is true.

findings.title: No test coverage for pagination boundaries
findings.explanation: The change touches pagination edge cases, and a test would have caught the off-by-one slice. Add tests for: fewer than `limit` rows, exactly `limit` rows (`next_before` is null), `limit + 1` rows (`next_before` is the last returned id), `limit=1`, and an empty result. Also check that no invoice is skipped or duplicated across consecutive pages.

Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
